workItems.title: Make real module and production-source tests the readiness evidence
workItems.rationale: In-profile module tests compile subsets, tautologies, standalone mirrors, or reimplemented models rather than loading the production libraries they claim to verify; experimental-module completion evidence is tracked separately. The production-source census and installed-template smoke are progress, not release proof. The module-evidence control plane now proves CMake target existence from a configure-generated CMake File API codemodel, rejects declared-but-unproduced evidence, has a real Windows lifecycle collector/host contract, and requires exact-SHA Windows lifecycle and installed-package-smoke producers before the Ubuntu consumer and aggregate gate. 2026-09-13 progress: the lifecycle consumer now rejects malformed or logger-prefixed duplicate marker lines instead of filtering them, with the full module-evidence suite green. 2026-09-14 progress: the local module-evidence wrapper now selects a runnable Python interpreter when the Windows Store python3 alias is present; its declarative/adversarial run completes with 307 tests and 12 expected skips. No hosted run has yet supplied the corresponding immutable lifecycle/package artifacts and successful required-gate evidence. Those unhosted proof gaps keep this item release-blocking. 2026-09-24 progress (local only; no hosted run yet): sanitizer-report is now required evidence for every included module (REQUIRED_INCLUDED_EVIDENCE) and is bound for SparkGameFPS. Its producer now points at the real run-sanitizer-tests.sh layout: build/module-evidence/sanitizer-asan/metadata.json plus the sibling junit.xml, from the test-results-linux-asan artifact. The previous binding was build/asan-ubsan-lsan-results.txt, which no workflow produced. module-evidence now needs build-linux-asan, runs verify-sanitizer-evidence.py verify-published on the downloaded directory, and the manifest consumer checks that the metadata commitSha equals the revision under test, the originEvidenceDirectory matches that SHA and the recorded runId/runAttempt, the run is clean (exact-all selector, zero exit, zero failures and errors, no sanitizer signals or runtime logs), junitSha256 matches the sibling junit.xml, the junit.xml records at least the 6900-testcase SparkTests floor (pinned by a test to the workflow's verify-published --minimum-tests), and at least one FPSRespawn_* test (production-source, registered in SparkTests) executed and passed. Binding the directory to the current workflow run id/attempt is done only by the preceding verify-published step. 32 tests (golden path in path and rooted mode, the shipped binding, producer layout, floor parity and selector census, plus 26 rejection cases) cover a missing file, the wrong SHA, a foreign origin or run identity, a below-floor clean run, a selector-free junit, a skipped selector, a failed selector, a swapped junit, the TSan lane and the stale path. A hosted exact-SHA ASan artifact consumed by module-evidence has not been observed.

workItems.title: Establish asset and package integrity manifests
workItems.rationale: Several modules reference missing music/models/scenes, depend on path case that differs from the tree, or work only through procedural fallbacks and repository-relative content. The asset-integrity CI job exists in site-data.yml, legacy per-package manifests remain validated, and a fail-closed first-party root integrity manifest is now tracked. 2026-09-12 progress: runtime packages now install Assets/assets.integrity.json under bin/Assets, and extracted-package validation rejects a missing, link-like, or tampered runtime asset manifest/payload using the repository verifier with case-correct paths. 2026-09-21 progress: the installed FPS profile-package smoke now stages the manifest's root README and verifies all 882 staged bin/Assets entries before module lifecycle and save/reload; adversarial helper tests reject missing manifests, missing or tampered payloads, exact-case mismatches, undeclared files, and link-like paths. The fail-closed module inventory covers all 11 GameModules, with FPS root Models/Scenes integrity coverage at 317/317; content outside the in-profile FPS root remains unclassified. 2026-09-23 local progress: the source and installed Release asset manifest now verify 883/883 entries, including the FPS center-building material; the package-layout smoke proves a controlled material albedo edit changes rendered pixels. 2026-09-23 local progress: the source and installed Release asset manifest now verify 883/883 entries, including the FPS center-building material; the package-layout smoke proves a controlled material albedo edit changes rendered pixels. 2026-09-24 local progress (OD-09): the stable-v1 runtime package (SparkGameFPS selector) now installs through cmake/SparkRuntimeAssets.cmake, which derives the stable-v1 manifest at configure time and excludes all 475 NOASSERTION TERRAFRONT entries (408 of 883 entries ship); verify --profile stable-v1 rejects any NOASSERTION, relabelled, unreviewed, or altered packaged entry and runs in the installed FPS package smoke and the release extracted-package check. The excluded files stay in the repository and their provenance stays open outside stable-v1. Clean Windows 11/archive, profile-wide package, provenance, exact-SHA proof, and remaining module content debt still remain open. 2026-09-24 local progress: tools/site-data/module_content.py now scans in-profile module sources (SparkGameFPS) after a single comment/literal-aware lexing pass (raw and prefixed strings included) and validate.py fails on any detected site not declared in GameModules/module-content-inventory.json fallbackSites with an intentional, gap, or tracked policy. Enforcement covers only three site shapes: calls to identifiers containing Fallback or Procedural, and LoadObj calls whose receiver names a different .obj than it loads; inline defaults without such a named helper are not detected. The WaveSpawner perimeter spawns were moved into the named MakeFallbackWaveSpawnPoints helper so they are enforced; the six current FPS sites are declared, and the shotgun/rocket/grenade rifle.obj substitutions are tracked under MOD-310, which owns the fix. 2026-09-25 local progress: Tests/TestAssetManifestReal.cpp adds the AssetManifest_* and PathCase_* selectors (CTest AssetManifest_FPSReferences and PathCase_FPSReferences, 2 tests each, --empty-is-error). The references are the asset-rooted string literals in GameModules/SparkGameFPS/Source (comment/include-aware lexing of the production files) plus every model/material the production SceneManager keeps for Scenes/level1.scene loaded through Spark::FPSAssets::Resolve; each must be declared in Assets/assets.integrity.json and resolve with byte-exact case per path component under both the repository root found by FindAssetRoot and the runtime Root(), and case-altered, traversal, absolute and drive spellings are rejected by the exact-case lookup and ResolveScenePath. Local mutation checks (a Models/Pistol.obj literal in Player.cpp, an Assets/materials/ spelling in level1.scene) fail both selectors. Coverage is the FPS module only; other modules and hosted exact-SHA evidence remain open. 2026-09-25 local progress: the stable-v1 package now installs only the SparkGameFPS runtime asset closure (40 of 883 entries) instead of every asset root. tools/asset-integrity/package_closure.py derives it from the asset-rooted string literals in the in-profile module sources (modules taken from GameModules/module-content-inventory.json and cross-checked against tools/asset-integrity/package-profiles.json) and in the reviewed engine source directory SparkEngine/Source (which adds the Models/{Cube,Plane,Sphere,Wall,Pyramid,Ramp}.obj defaults the engine primitive objects load when FPS or SceneManager creates them), the reviewed seeds there (asset README, Engine/Branding), and the scenes/materials those reference transitively. A literal counts as a reference when its first component names a top-level asset directory ignoring case (backslashes and a leading ./ or Assets/ normalised); an unresolved or case-mismatched reference, or a closure entry whose license is NOASSERTION, fails configure. The only exemptions are 13 reviewed unshippedReferences (the DecalSystem .dds names no code opens and the EntityPresetManager preset strings only the editor reads; none exists in the tree), each with a reason, and a stale or asset-shadowing exemption also fails. The closure covers literal asset paths only; paths composed at run time are not derived, so it is not yet proven to be everything the D3D11 runtime opens. verify --profile stable-v1 now also rejects a package that ships a file outside the closure (profile-outside-closure) or omits a closure file (profile-incomplete), and derives the closure from the verifier's own checkout (or fails with profile-closure) when the source manifest sits outside a tree with the profile definitions; the previous NOASSERTION-only stable-v1 layout (408 entries) fails with 368 profile-outside-closure errors. Configure re-derives the closure when the profile definition, inventory, a followed scene/material, or the set of scanned source files changes; an edit inside an existing source file does not reconfigure, and the resulting stale package is rejected by verify as profile-incomplete. check-all --profile stable-v1 --strict-provenance passes (40/40 license-asserted) while the whole-repository --strict-provenance still fails on 475 NOASSERTION entries. ValidateStagedPackageExecutables.cmake requires bin/Assets/Scenes/level1.scene for stable-v1 instead of the TERRAFRONT MMOFPS/Data/continents.json. Linux runtime proof: the closure staged by the real cmake/SparkRuntimeAssets.cmake rules plus the built SparkEngine and libSparkGameFPS.so reports SPARK_MODULE_READY count=1 and a clean SparkGameFPS lifecycle, headless and windowed under Xvfb with NullRHI, and strace shows no asset access outside the staged tree (that run used the earlier 34-entry closure, before the engine primitive OBJs were added). The Linux FPS player skips weapon and scene meshes without a D3D11 device, so NullRHI cannot show mesh loads and the Windows package smoke (MOD-310) must confirm the D3D11 model/material/texture loads match the closure; no hosted exact-SHA evidence exists.

workItems.title: Repair fail-closed required CI
workItems.rationale: ASan/TSan pipelines can mask failing test processes, MinGW/Wine cannot run under current triggers, and coverage, validation, format, and static-analysis surfaces are incomplete or advisory. 2026-09-05 progress: the advisory-lane derivation landed in the exact-source gate (a failed Build job is accepted only if build.yml at that exact commit declares continue-on-error; required set cross-checked against EXPECTED_REQUIRED_JOBS_JSON; a required job marked continue-on-error is rejected). 2026-09-08 read-only remote evidence for Working 891e00c1cb4a930a38e61da26e62f56d4af88de3: its Build Matrix Verifier rejected the exact producer artifact because the producer reported 3 parity errors while the Linux trusted checker reported 19. The 16-error difference is a cross-host path-semantics defect in the old checker, which interpreted Windows-recorded paths with host Path/os.path rules. Local canonical commit 9583053edabdae37af6f737132bfc50eefd92930 uses recorded Windows/POSIX path semantics and restricts verifier sources to Working push/workflow_dispatch, but has not been published or proven by an exact-SHA remote run. Verified 2026-09-12 that legacy branch protection remains absent on Working (branches/Working/protection is 404), while repository ruleset 21968740 (Working integrity) is active and requires the GitHub Actions Required CI Gate check with no bypass actors. 2026-09-13 progress: the required-job verifier now fails closed when EXPECTED_REQUIRED_JOBS_JSON is missing or empty, with focused and failure-propagation regressions green. 2026-09-13 additional progress: the TODO/FIXME threshold now emits an error and exits nonzero, and the Windows registration guard now prefers Git Bash and passes POSIX script paths; focused CI policy suites pass locally. 2026-09-14 progress: the failure-propagation contract now verifies that workflow_dispatch reaches every required job and the always-running Required CI Gate without event/ref skips or cancellation; the full local contract suite passes 78/78. 2026-09-14 additional progress: build.yml now exposes an explicit, default-off workflow_dispatch control that fails the required validate-ci-tools job, and the workflow regression suite covers its manual-only guard. 2026-09-21 further progress: exact hosted failure showed a registered fuzz test without a built executable; the workflow now builds all three fuzz targets, and structural policy enforces target completeness plus build-before-CTest across 162 tests. The same hosted run exposed Windows newline drift in the crash-manifest corpus; those exact seed bytes are now LF-pinned and pass in an isolated core.autocrlf=true checkout. Exact SHA 37a4bec5 subsequently passed Site Data, CodeQL, Microsoft C++ analysis, and Trusted Reporter, while the main Build correctly failed on a portable temporary-directory assumption, platform-native cooker fixture newlines, and non-artifact CMake target semantics; bounded local fixes are covered by focused policy suites. The corrected SHA still needs hosted proof. Item stays open until an exact-SHA hosted control run proves the required-job failure turns Required CI Gate red. 2026-09-24 progress (local only; no hosted run of these changes yet): (1) the exact-source verifier (verify-exact-required-gate.py) accepted a non-success Build job only if it was continue-on-error, so every Working push, where build-linux-mingw-wine and Coverage PR Comment are always skipped, would have been rejected. It now also accepts a skipped non-required job whose exact committed job-level if: is on a closed allowlist of event-only guards (workflow_dispatch-only, pull_request-only) that is false for the verified event. Real-build.yml regressions and mutations cover a skipped required job, a guard that is true for the event, an unrecognised or widened if:, and a duplicate if:. (2) build-linux-mingw-wine is now named 'build-linux-mingw-wine (experimental)' with job-level continue-on-error: true, which the docs already claimed. A structural test with mutations locks it as dispatch-only, advisory and outside the required gate. Hosted run 34983218822 (PR branch claude/stable-v1-release, 3f427dd, job 104483285541) built under MinGW, then failed Run Tests under Wine. extract-errors counted 32 test failures, including CrashHandler_UngatedReportWritesAnArtifactAndTheAssertGateDoesNot (private crash-artifact directory creation failed under Wine) and an ACCESS_VIOLATION in AudioEngineReal_PooledVoiceIsRebuiltForANewSoundFormat inside Wine FAudio with no ALSA card. These are recorded on the MinGW wiki page, and no tests are excluded. (3) validate-ci-tools now runs check-pragma-once, check-editor-panels, check-deprecated-submodules, check-wiki-nav, check-wiring, check-doxygen-coverage, check-cross-utilization and check-di-singletons fail-closed. test-workflow-failure-propagation.py maps every tools/validate-all.sh run_check to a required invocation or a reasoned advisory entry (check-bloat, check-wiki-quality). (4) .github/scripts/verify-working-ruleset.py checks ruleset 21968740 from a captured 2026-09-24 API fixture (tested in validate-ci-tools) or --live. A live run on 2026-09-24 returned ok: active, no bypass actors, deletion + non_fast_forward, and exactly 'Required CI Gate' from integration 15368. Still open: the Working-branch controlled red run, exact-SHA acceptance of a Working push by the verifiers, a docs-only Working gate summary, a hosted MinGW dispatch after labeling, and exact-SHA artifacts. 2026-09-24 additional progress (local only): verify-required-jobs.py gained --json-out, which writes a canonical sparkengine.required-ci-gate.v1 record (sha, run id/attempt, repository, event, ref, expected jobs, per-job results, deferred entries, verdict) on both pass and fail without changing the exit code, and writes nothing (removing any stale record) when the needs evidence or run identity is invalid. Required CI Gate uploads it under if: always() as required-ci-gate-<sha>-<attempt> with if-no-files-found: error; test-verify-required-jobs.py covers failed, skipped, missing, deferred, malformed and identity cases and test-workflow-failure-propagation.py mutation-checks that the upload survives a red gate. No hosted run has published the record yet, so no consumer depends on it.

workItems.title: Enforce deterministic test, coverage, sanitizer, and static-analysis policy
workItems.rationale: One monolithic CTest registration, warning-tolerated flaky patterns, nonblocking thresholds, missing golden baselines, and partial clang-tidy/CodeQL coverage prevent a green result from proving release quality. 2026-09-05 progress: SparkTests is split into SparkEngineTests and SparkEngineLoadTests (labels load;slow) with per-configuration timeout budgets; the runner reports [ EMPTY ] tests and flaky waivers explicitly (EXPECT_WARN_ONLY, EXPECT_NO_CRASH, SKIP_TEST) and JUnit carries flaky=/empty= attributes; SPARK_TESTS_WARN_IS_ERROR exists but defaults OFF because Tests/TestWarnings.h still holds 8 waivers documenting real non-determinism. 2026-09-12 progress: the clang-tidy lane now inventories every shipped-product source root and fails closed on missing roots or an empty translation-unit inventory instead of analyzing a capped sample. 2026-09-13 progress: coverage enforcement now requires test, generation, and threshold steps to end exactly in success and rejects skipped/cancelled evidence, with direct workflow regressions. 2026-09-13 additional progress: Tools/validate_test_warnings.py now requires exact registry/metadata parity, named owners, and future ISO expiries for all whole-test waivers; blocking CI runs the validator and 7 adversarial policy tests. 2026-09-21 further progress: the exact hosted failure was a registered fuzz test without a built executable; the workflow now builds all three fuzz targets and structural policy enforces target completeness plus build-before-CTest across 162 tests. Executable-level smokes now exercise SparkConsole batch dispatch, SparkCrashReporter failure semantics, a two-pass SparkCooker manifest, real D3D11 shader compilation, SparkAutomation through the FPS NullRHI lifecycle, SparkBuild plan generation, and SparkEditor project load/clean shutdown. workItems.rationale: Release automation already generates SHA256SUMS, an SBOM, and build attestations. Stable-v1 still requires independently verified code signing, artifact and dependency scan policy, and a protected release approval environment; existing integrity metadata alone does not satisfy this gate. A bounded first slice now gates final stable Windows Runtime EXE/MSI execution and upload on native Valid embedded Authenticode, a timestamp certificate, an explicitly configured publisher certificate thumbprint, and SHA-256 continuity through native qualification. Injected-process regressions run in validate-ci-tools; real unsigned EXE/MSI fixture rejection is wired to ordinary Windows VS 2022 Release CI and the Windows stable release job. 2026-09-13 progress: native signature evidence and persisted reports now reject duplicate JSON keys instead of accepting last-write-wins contradictions. 2026-09-13 additional progress: signature report publication and hash verification now reject symlinked report paths and publish through an atomic no-replace boundary, with 7 focused signature tests. 2026-09-21 progress: stable publication now has a fail-closed consumer verifier for the exact asset set, SHA256SUMS, nonempty SPDX payload coverage, exact-CI provenance, pinned trusted-key fingerprint, and real OpenSSL detached signatures. Its externally provisioned signature archive is digest-pinned, flat regular-file-only, Windows-name-safe, and reverified before both draft creation and promotion. Local cryptographic, archive, workflow, and failure-propagation suites pass. 2026-09-24 progress: the release job now scans the generated SPDX SBOM with a SHA-pinned anchore/scan-action (grype, JSON) before asset collection and draft staging, and .github/scripts/verify_vulnerability_findings.py blocks the release on any Critical/High finding not covered by a current exception in ThirdParty/supply-chain.lock whose id names the advisory and whose scope is vulnerability:<package>, and on expired, unused, or malformed exceptions, an empty SBOM, or a failed or incomplete scan. Findings grype suppressed into ignoredMatches (a .grype.yaml ignore rule, VEX, only-fixed) are gated like matches, a scan run with only-fixed/only-notfixed/ignore-states/VEX/exclude settings, with the stock matcher's CPE matching disabled, with any of those settings absent from the report's configuration, or with a grype config file in the checkout fails, and the release.yml contract allow-lists the scan-action inputs and rejects GRYPE_* env, run defaults or working-directory on the scan/gate steps, and gate-step env, and requires the tokenized gate invocation to pass exactly --report/--sbom/--lockfile/--summary once each with the expected values, rejecting --today/--checkout, repeated options, and trailing shell; the gate CLI refuses abbreviated options. The exception schema is the one tools/check-supply-chain.py enforces (factored into validate_exception_records). CTest ArtifactIntegrity_VulnerabilityGate covers fixture reports on every lane; its release.yml wiring cases run only where PyYAML is installed and are enforced in CI by the check-supply-chain 'Release vulnerability gate tests' step; no hosted scan against the live grype database has run, and whether syft's SBOM of the packaged C++ binaries catalogs the statically linked ThirdParty components is unverified, so dependency-level scanning stays with SEC-110, which should reuse this gate. 2026-09-24 release-approval progress: the stable release job now runs .github/scripts/record_release_approval.py immediately after the environment-protection gate. It reads GET /repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/approvals with bounded, Link-paginated, duplicate-key-rejecting, fail-closed HTTP, binds the history to the exact run attempt, head SHA, release workflow path, repository and stable-release environment id, and requires at least one approved review, every review approved by the repository owner Krilliac (login and id) for stable-release only, and no rejected review. It publishes a closed, deterministic record (run id/attempt/start, environment, approver, per-review comment SHA-256) with no-replace semantics, retains it as a 90-day workflow artifact, and exports its SHA-256 as a job output. verify_published_stable_release.py now requires that digest, independently rebuilds the record from the API, refuses on any mismatch before downloading assets, and embeds the approval in the consumer receipt. CTest ReleaseApproval_Record (17 tests, injected urlopen) and the extended consumer suite (34 tests) pass locally. The approvals API exposes no review timestamp, so the record bounds approval time by the run start and the artifact upload; how GitHub reports a sole-owner self-approval still needs a hosted stable run, and an owner-only approval is not an independent second-person review. Publisher key/signature-bundle provisioning, a hosted protected approval, native signed-artifact success evidence, a hosted vulnerability scan, and hosted exact-SHA proof remain prerequisites; REL-110 is open.

workItems.title: Rehearse and approve the qualified release candidate before publication
workItems.rationale: Technical rehearsal, qualification sign-off, and release approval must finish before publication. This item retains all former REL-200 prepublication requirements, including their unimplemented jobs/selectors. It is never a publication-finalization exemption. The signed v0.9.0 predecessor and live immutable-channel publication remain unproven; neither can be replaced with synthetic evidence. 2026-09-24 progress: tools/release_notes.py now renders the stable RELEASE_BODY (release.yml step 'Render fail-closed stable release notes', after the signature bundle and before draft staging) from the stable-v1 profile in docs/site/readiness.json (support matrix, supported hosts, experimental/unsupported capabilities, excluded gates, limitations verbatim), the single CHANGELOG.md [X.Y.Z] section and its migration subsection, the frozen SHA256SUMS lines, and fixed sha256sum/openssl/gh attestation verification instructions with the pinned signer fingerprint. It fails closed on a missing or duplicated version section, empty or inconsistent SHA256SUMS, an SBOM or SHA256SUMS absent from the expected asset list, or a missing signature control asset whose public key does not match the pinned fingerprint.
